method: Initial manual testing followed by fixes, regression tests, deterministic chart renders, and further interaction through Bitrig's iPad and Watch simulators. Initial observations are preserved below.
overallResult: Failed checks reproduced; full coverage incomplete because simulator inspection stopped working.

environment.runtimeOSVersions: Not provided by simulator observations; SDK and deployment targets were inspected separately.

buildChanges.reason: Bitrig blocked simulator interactions until all runnable targets built successfully; the existing Mac build failed.
changes: Raised the Mac app, widget, and test deployment targets from 26.5 to 27.0 with user approval.
Applied navigationBar visibility modifiers only on platforms that support navigationBar.
Used a sheet for the existing full-screen presentation routes on Mac.
Restricted the embedded Watch app and its target dependency to iOS.
buildChanges.validation: Bitrig build_project returned success after the fixes and again on the subsequent rebuild. git diff --check passed.
buildChanges.laterRecoveryBuild: Subsequent build_project calls completed successfully. iPad interaction recovered; iPhone state inspection still fails.

passedChecks.verified: Read all three pages using Next, then tapped Start journaling and reached Today.
Selected Wink in Today and Sad in Page. Entered and replaced notes through the software keyboard; draft status updated. The other three mood choices were visible but were not individually exercised.
Writing about a walk and family produced peaceful walk, family, grateful, and outdoors suggestions. Selecting grateful and family updated the tag count and chips.
passedChecks.limit: This verifies the suggestion UI, not whether Apple Intelligence or the existing fallback generated the suggestions.

passedChecks.verified: Save changed to disabled Saved; the note, mood, and selected tags appeared in Recent pages and a calendar sticker appeared in Page.
A downward content drag dismissed the keyboard and restored access to the tab bar. Save alone left the keyboard open.
Tapping the October 4 calendar sticker loaded the saved note into the Page editor.
Changed the saved note, chose Sad, added calm, and tapped Save page. Recent pages and Insights reflected the edit.
Wink showed zero matching pages, Sad showed the edited page, and All restored browsing without a mood restriction.
The single saved Sad entry produced Entries 1, Average 2.0, a trend point at Sad, and a Sad distribution count of 1.
With zero or one saved entry, the recap explained that at least two entries were required rather than displaying a generation failure.
Switched repeatedly among Today, Page, and Insights after dismissing the keyboard.

findings.title: Today retains stale saved state after a Page edit
steps: In Page, tap its calendar sticker, edit its note and mood, and save.
findings.expected: Today's editor displays the current saved entry when it has no unsaved changes.
findings.actual: Today still shows the original Wink mood and original note with disabled Saved, while its Recent pages card shows the edited Sad entry.
findings.risk: A subsequent Today save could replace the newer Page edit. That overwrite was not executed during this test.
findings.source: MoodMargins/Features/Today/ViewModel/TodayViewModel.swift: loadTodayIfNeeded only loads once per view-model lifecycle.
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Clean Today editors refresh from value snapshots; unsaved drafts remain independent. Deleting a saved page clears a clean editor.
findings.verification: JournalSynchronizationTests covers external edits, draft preservation, and deletion. The same saved note was visible in Today and Pages on iPad.

findings.title: Page starts with a template instead of today's saved entry
steps: Open Page before tapping a calendar sticker.
findings.expected: The selected date and editor agree with the saved entry, or the UI explicitly presents a separate new draft.
findings.actual: The editor shows Dear diary, and the default Laughing mood even though a saved Wink entry exists for the displayed date. Tapping its calendar sticker loads the real entry.
findings.risk: Save page can replace the entry for the displayed date with this template. The replacement behavior is inferred from the save implementation; the template overwrite was not executed.
findings.source: MoodMargins/Features/Pages/ViewModel/PageViewModel.swift: default draft values and same-day fallback save matching.
findings.initialStatus: Stale initial editor reproduced; overwrite risk identified from code.
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Pages synchronizes its initial selection with the saved entry, with an empty draft only when no entry exists.
findings.verification: Initial editor loading was observed on iPad. An isolated SwiftData regression test verifies that saving this initial state preserves the existing note and mood.

findings.title: Dark appearance makes diary text and secondary labels unreadable
findings.expected: Readable text contrast against the diary cards and background in both appearances.
findings.actual: Diary notes become white on cream cards. Dates, status copy, insight captions, and chart dates become very faint on the fixed light backgrounds.
findings.initialStatus: Reproduced on Today and Insights; not fixed.
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Diary backgrounds, ink, secondary ink, and rules use appearance-aware colors; controls use native tint.
findings.verification: Light and dark Insights were visually inspected on iPad, including maximum accessibility text size. Compact dark chart fixtures were rendered separately.

findings.title: Insights shows the Today heading and no range selector
steps: Open Insights and inspect the entire screen.
findings.expected: An Insights heading and a reachable control for the supported ranges.
findings.actual: The heading is Today. No range picker appears visually or in the accessibility tree; the screen remains on the 7-day range.
findings.source: InsightsView uses Header rather than the existing InsightHeader, which contains the range picker.
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Insights uses InsightHeader and a 7/14/30/365-day range picker, changing to a menu at accessibility text sizes.
findings.verification: The 7-day and 14-day graphs and selected controls were observed on iPad. Unit tests cover all selectable ranges.

findings.title: Insight summaries display raw symbol names and unsupported conclusions
steps: Save a Sad entry and inspect Insights again.
findings.expected: A friendly empty state, a meaningful common-mood value, and patterns supported by the saved entries.
findings.actual: Most common displays angry.face with no entries and sad.face after the edit. The empty screen shows #calm as Top tag. Soft pattern claims outdoors pages often have Good or Great moods even with no entries or outdoors tags.
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Most common uses its live Lottie emoji; empty summaries show dashes, and patterns derive from actual saved tags and moods.
findings.verification: Most common Laughing, empty Top tag, factual empty activity state, and real distribution counts were observed on iPad. Pattern and empty-state rules have regression coverage.

findings.title: The streak badge is static
steps: Finish onboarding on the empty simulator and inspect Today and Insights.
findings.expected: A streak derived from saved entries.
findings.actual: Both screens display 3-day streak with zero entries, and the badge remains unchanged after one save.
findings.initialStatus: Reproduced and confirmed in code; not fixed.
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Streak counts unique consecutive saved calendar days, allowing an unfinished today.
findings.verification: A real 1-day streak was observed on iPad. Fixed-calendar tests cover duplicate entries, gaps, yesterday, empty data, and future entries.

findings.title: Search is not reachable on the tested Page screen
steps: Open Page and inspect its header, browsing section, and accessibility tree.
findings.expected: A visible or discoverable search control for saved pages.
findings.actual: No search field or search action was available despite searchable being declared in the view.
findings.initialStatus: Control absence observed; query behavior could not be tested.
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Pages exposes its search field and matches localized note, tag, and mood text with whitespace trimming.
findings.verification: Search was visible on iPad. A nonmatching query returned zero pages; park returned the saved page. The search was cleared afterward.

findings.title: Maximum Dynamic Type breaks labels and saved-page previews
steps: Inspect Today and scroll to Recent pages.
findings.expected: Readable controls and meaningful preview text at supported accessibility sizes.
findings.actual: Saved breaks within the word across lines. The small Recent pages card reduces the date and note to heavily truncated fragments such as Oc… and UI T….
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Save controls reflow, preview width and typography scale, dates adapt, and accessibility layouts use a single column without excessive minimum card height.
findings.verification: Large-text iPad controls and Insights layouts were inspected. Compact and accessibility chart fixtures rendered successfully. A final iPhone replay remains blocked by Bitrig state inspection.

findings.title: Selected moods and tags are not conveyed in accessibility state
steps: Select a mood and tags, then inspect their accessibility entries.
findings.expected: The selected state is available to assistive technology as well as visually.
findings.actual: The controls expose labels but no selected trait or selected-state value after selection, while their visual styling changes.
findings.initialStatus: Accessibility tree observation only; VoiceOver interaction was not completed.
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Mood controls expose selected traits; tag controls use native Toggle state. Decorative emojis are hidden from VoiceOver while chart points and distribution rows expose mood descriptions.
findings.verification: The iPad accessibility tree showed the selected Laughing mood and native tag switch state. VoiceOver operation itself was not completed.

findings.title: The Watch app is still a placeholder
findings.expected: Usable MoodMargins functionality on the shipped Watch target.
findings.actual: Only a globe and Hello, world! appear. There are no journaling controls.
findings.initialStatus: Reproduced; not implemented during this testing task.
findings.status: Fixed; validation and remaining limits are described below.
findings.remediation: Watch has a native mood picker, note field, same-day save/edit, recent pages, and local persisted storage with explicit local-only copy.
findings.verification: Watch showed a saved mood and note after rebuilding. An isolated persistence harness verified save, reopening, same-day edit without duplication, and protection of unreadable storage. Phone sync is not implemented or advertised.

inconclusiveObservations.flow: iPhone landscape with Reduce Motion enabled
inconclusiveObservations.observed: Page appeared in a narrow column with blank white side areas. Simulator inspection subsequently failed.
inconclusiveObservations.limit: The observation was not reproduced on another device; it may be a simulator rendering problem rather than an app layout defect. Reduce Motion animation behavior was not established.

Verified cold-launch persistence of the main journal, CloudKit synchronization between devices, and real save-error recovery.

followUpValidation.build: Final Bitrig build_project succeeded with no diagnostics after the endpoint date-label fix.
followUpValidation.tests: xcodebuild test on macOS with Xcode 27: 17 XCTest tests plus 32 Swift Testing tests passed (49 total). The chart rendering test was rerun after the final endpoint-label adjustment and passed.
followUpValidation.renderLimits: ImageRenderer cannot flatten the platform-backed Lottie player. Animated emojis were verified in the live iPad app rather than inferred from static renders.
graphChanges: Vertical-axis Lottie emojis retained; numbered mood legend removed.
Mood Stickers distribution labels and Most Common use live Lottie emojis, retaining accessible mood names.
Overall mood uses descriptive words instead of an unexplained numeric average; a balanced 3.5 remains a mix of moods.
Trend points use actual calendar dates, preserve missing-day gaps, and show endpoint date labels aligned inside the plot.
Distribution bars show share of all saved pages, with zero-count bars empty.
Cards use consistent upright layouts, equal summary widths, dynamic appearance colors, and adaptive columns.
modelChanges: Production Foundation Models code directly targets OS 27; availability-version wrappers and fallback generators were removed.
A persisted picker chooses on-device SystemLanguageModel or PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel for both tags and recaps, defaulting to on-device.
OS 27 sessions check readiness, locale, guided-generation capability, and PCC quota; typed network, quota, and service failures expose recovery instructions.
Generation is streamed in cancellable view-owned tasks. Request identities include model choice and note edits; failed requests can be retried.
The live picker exposed both options. On-device tag suggestions appeared for the existing iPad note. No live PCC generation was performed.
